request.spec:
Show on each person their cut total: their cuts across every pool they are a member of, added
up (a pool that shows no cuts adds nothing). Show the sheet's cut total: everyone's added up.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show on each person their cut total: their cuts across every pool they are a member of, added
up (a pool that shows no cuts adds nothing). Show the sheet's cut total: everyone's added up.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person now shows a cut total, and the sheet shows a total cut for everyone. All 4 acceptance tests pass under `bin/e2e`.

The whole change is in `src/main/frontend/features/pools/pools.slot.tsx`. I didn't need to change the server or the stored data.

- **Per person (`person-cut-total`):** a new "Cut" column in the people table. It adds up the person's cuts in every pool they're directly in. A pool that is unbalanced or has no pot shows a blank cut, so it adds nothing.
- **Sheet (`rollup-cut-total`):** a "Cut in all" line next to the other sheet totals, adding up every person's cut total.

The totals reuse the cuts the server already works out for the pools list. A pool that sits inside another pool doesn't count for anyone. Only the people in it do, through their own cuts there.

The sheet total is a plain sum of the per-person figures, not the pot. In the first test it shows 20.00 against a pot of 10.00, because Ada is in more than one pool. That is what the test expects.
